## SECTION 12 — FULL RS2 ANALYSIS & FINAL EXECUTION OPINION

### 12.1 Valuation Engine Selection

**Engine chosen: 12.2 Two-Stage DCF (FCFF → Equity).** Rationale:

1. The pack holds 12 years of fiscal-year income/cash-flow data — enough to build full projections.
2. The recent business inflection (2025 $886M → 2026E ~$1.9B, +114% guided) renders any single trailing multiple meaningless.
3. The massive 2026 working-capital build and $1.15B convertible issuance must be modeled explicitly — only a DCF handles this.
4. The 20-F filer status (no TTM) favors clean fiscal-year projections over trailing data.

**Cash-flow definition**: FCFF = NOPAT + D&A − Capex − ΔOperating Working Capital (ex-cash), where NOPAT = GAAP Operating Income × (1 − 22% tax rate). SBC is **not added back** — it is treated as a real expense (confirmed by pack warning). We use GAAP operating margins, which include SBC.

### 12.2 Discount Rate Derivation

| Equity risk premium | 4.75% | Analyst assumption given inflation/rate uncertainty — [Assumption] |

| Pre-tax cost of debt | 0.00% | Convert bears no coupon; no accretion — [Actual] |
| Debt weight | D/(D+E) = 1.15 / (8.67 + 1.15) = 11.7% | Market values |
| **WACC** | 0.883 × 12.83% + 0.117 × 0% × (1−0.22) = **11.34% → 11.5%** | Rounded conservatively |

*Note: The 0% coupon makes debt effectively free in a static WACC, but the conversion option and refinancing risk justify rounding WACC up to 11.5%.*

### 12.9 Critical Uncertainties (Must be carried, not buried)

1. **Convertible proceeds deployment** — if the $1.15B is spent on NAND prepayments that later prove not to convert to revenue (cancellation clauses, quality issues), net debt rises and FCF suffers. **[Unconfirmed]**

# SECTION 1 — BUSINESS & QUALITATIVE POSITION

## 1.1 What the company does

Silicon Motion designs and sells NAND flash controllers — the firmware/ASIC that manages every SSD and embedded storage device — across four product families:

- **Client SSD controllers** (PCIe/SATA) for PCs and consumer SSDs — sold to NAND makers and module makers
- **Embedded controllers (eMMC/UFS)** for smartphones, IoT, automotive — SIMO is the dominant *merchant* supplier of these
- **Enterprise SSD controllers (MonTitan, PCIe 4/5)** for AI servers and data centers — the new growth engine — competing against Marvell and Phison
- **FerriSSD and boot drives** for automotive, industrial, and now **AI server boot storage** (~30% of revenue in Q2 2026, up from 4% a year earlier [Actual — Q2 transcript])

Fabless, Taiwan-headquartered (Milpitas CA listing), sells to Samsung, SK Hynix, Kioxia, Micron, Phison and module makers. Fiscal year = calendar year (derived from "year ended December 31, 2025" [Actual — press release title]).

## 1.2 Competitive position — my assessment

The pack's web brief sources claim a "strong moat" but with **"ROIC of 0.1% and gross margin of 0.5%"** — those fraction-figures are aggregator errors; the filed numbers are gross margin 48.3% and roughly 10–20% ROIC depending on year. The moat is thinner in client SSD controllers where PCIe 4→5 migration has been slower than expected due to OEM cost sensitivity [Actual — transcript]. - **NAND supply scarcity until 2028** (management: new fabs not online until then) — gives pricing power but limits unit growth [Actual — transcript]

# SECTION 7 — RISKS

## 7.1 Risks to the bear case (things that could drive the price down)

1. **Cyclical bust (the dominant risk).** SIMO has produced a −6%, −14%, and −32% revenue year in the last decade, always after a boom. The 2026 +100% boom is the largest yet. NAND supply normalizes in 2028 per management's own words, and NAND makers who currently outsource controllers will have a strong incentive to re-integrate when they have idle internal capacity — the exact reversal of the current tailwind.
2. **Negative free cash flow in 2026.** My model has 2026 FCF ≈ +$8M only after a heroic $980M capital raise. If ΔWC exceeds ~$280M (Q2's $80M quarterly burn escalates), the company will consume the entire $980M proceed before 2028 and need further financing or slower growth — compressing value.
3. **The $1B convertible creates a 2031 cash obligation.** If the stock does not exceed $380.50, the company must repay $1B in cash in 2031 (or on the 2029 put date). My model assumes $700M+ FCF by 2031 makes this manageable — but FCF could be much lower in the bear case.
4. **Customer concentration.** The pack holds no segment/customer data. Historically SIMO's top customers (NAND makers, Phison) have been a large share of revenue — a fact my research could not re-establish because Q&A transcripts are not in the pack. [Unconfirmed — treat as a real risk]
5. **Competition in enterprise controllers.** Marvell, Phison, and newly-acquired in-house SSD controller teams at NAND manufacturers (the 2015–2020 M&A wave flagged in the web brief) all target MonTitan's market.
6. **Taiwan geopolitical risk.** The pack data ends at the balance sheet; this risk is real but not quantifiable from the pack, and I have only a modest premium in the 11% WACC.

## 7.2 Risks to the bull case (things that could drive the price up)

1. The AI-server boot-drive + MonTitan ramp exceeds even management's 2026 "double" guidance, with 2027 growth above 30%.
2. Operating margins reach 30%+ on a *sustained* basis (not just an exit rate), driven by enterprise mix.
3. The robotics/physical-AI Ferri opportunity ("may be larger than automotive") opens a new S-curve in 2027–2029.
4. Working-capital conversion improves faster than my model — inventory turns accelerate, receivables monetize, releasing cash.
5. The NAND outsourcing wave becomes structural (NAND makers never rebuild in-house controller teams), supporting my base-case 2028–2030 revenue.
